public_rationale: Part of the claim holds. Evidence for the 'lots of hype, little significant return' reading is solid. In WRITER's survey (fieldwork Dec 2025 to Jan 2026), only 23% of leaders said they had seen significant ROI from AI agents, and 48% called AI adoption a massive disappointment. In June 2025 a Gartner analyst said most agentic AI offerings lacked significant value or ROI and were mostly driven by hype. Against that, PwC's May 2025 survey found that two-thirds of agent adopters reported measurable productivity value. Google Cloud's 2025 study reported positive ROI among early adopters. So the answer depends on the bar. On significant ROI, the claim holds. On any measurable value, most adopters say they see some. Marcus gave no threshold, so I grade it mixed rather than supported or contradicted.
limitations: All the evidence is self-reported survey data, and much of it comes from vendors that sell AI or agents.
The PwC and Google figures are from mid-2025, while the WRITER figure is from early 2026. Timing may explain part of the gap.
The McKinsey and Gartner primary pages could not be read directly.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: So far, AI agents appear to have lots of hype but little return on investment, as with generative AI generally.

statement.excerpt: The situation for agents thus far looks to be similar: lots of hype; not so much ROI:

from_speaker: The situation for agents thus far
similar to the MIT finding that ROI for generative AI wasn't there for most businesses
our_interpretation: Plain reading: up to the post date, most businesses that tried AI agents had not seen significant or clear return on investment, even though agents were heavily promoted.
He named no study or threshold, so I read 'not so much ROI' as 'a minority of adopters report significant returns', judged by broad enterprise surveys and analyst assessments.
Target period: 2025-01 to the post date (2026-05-08). This covers the period when enterprise agent deployments and surveys about them appeared. 'Thus far' names no start date.
criteria.support_condition: Broad surveys or analyst reports from 2025 to May 2026 show that only a minority of organizations report significant or clear ROI from AI agents, or say most agent projects lack clear value.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Broad surveys or analyst reports from the same period show that most organizations using agents report clear, measurable returns from them.

evidence.excerpt: Still, few leaders say they’ve seen significant ROI from generative AI (29%) or AI agents (23%), and nearly half (48%) feel that AI adoption at their company has been a massive disappointment.
evidence.locator: section 'The top AI adoption challenges facing the C-suite', Lagging ROI bullet
evidence.explanation: In a survey of 2,400 workers and executives (fieldwork Dec 2025 to Jan 2026), only 23% of leaders reported significant ROI from AI agents. This fits 'not so much ROI' for agents and matches the pattern for gen AI. The publisher is a vendor that sells agents.

evidence.excerpt: "Most agentic AI propositions lack significant value or return on investment, as current models do not have the maturity and agency to autonomously achieve complex business goals or follow nuanced instructions over time," Verma said.
evidence.explanation: A Gartner analyst said most agentic AI offerings lacked significant value or ROI. In the same piece she said most projects were 'mostly driven by hype'. This supports both halves of the claim for mid-2025.

evidence.excerpt: Seventy-nine percent say AI agents are already being adopted in their companies. And of those adopting AI agents, two-thirds (66%) say that they’re delivering measurable value through increased productivity.
evidence.locator: section 'Key trends about AI agents in the enterprise', paragraph 2
evidence.explanation: Two-thirds of US agent adopters said agents deliver measurable productivity value. That cuts against 'not so much ROI' if any measurable value counts. PwC also says this 'stops short of transformation'. The available_at date is approximate: the page says the survey ran in May 2025.

evidence.excerpt: The second annual AI ROI study reveals 88% of agentic AI early adopters achieve positive return on investment, with 52% of generative AI organizations now deploying AI agents in production environments
evidence.explanation: A secondary summary of Google Cloud's vendor study reports high positive ROI among agent 'early adopters', who made up a minority of respondents. Other coverage says the figure refers to gen AI ROI on at least one use case, so I treat it as context only.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: An independent, large-sample study before May 2026 that measures financial returns (not self-reported value) from enterprise AI agent deployments against a stated threshold.
